assessments.reasoning: The raw intervals bind the introduction to the original PDF. Its opening identifies SETL as the implemented language. The later paragraph identifies LITTLE as the language used to build the NYU system and qualifies the implementation's coverage of the March 1980 reference.

challenge.method: Check whether the relationship reverses the two languages or implies exact conformance to Dewar's 1979 text.
challenge.results: The manual assigns distinct roles to SETL and LITTLE and enumerates deviations from its 1980 reference. These qualifications preserve the documented implementation relationship.

limitations: The manual refers to the March 1980 SETL reference and lists deviations. No exact conformance to Dewar's 1979 text is asserted.
The relation is from the SETL language identity to Shields's documented implementation. Matching the v30 system to the exact bytes of Dewar's ©1979 copy would require separate edition evidence.
